target_customer: High-end restaurants, mainly in Latin America, that want reservations, deposits and guest and revenue management
problem: Top restaurants lose money on no-shows and poorly allocated tables and pay commissions on marketplace bookings. Meitre offers reservation software with deposits, card guarantees and table allocation.
business_model: B2B SaaS for restaurants (one vendor profile says zero commission on reservations, unverified)
product_category: Restaurant reservation and revenue management software

founders.name: Juan Caviglia
founders.background_notes: Brother of Luis Caviglia per Contxto. YC page gives no professional background.

founders.name: Luis Caviglia
founders.background_notes: Contxto identifies Juan and Luis Caviglia as brothers and founders.

competitors.name: OpenTable
competitors.what: Dominant online restaurant reservation marketplace; YC's W18 batch post uses it as the comparison for Meitre
competitors.funding_then: Public company then, not stated in the source

technical_complexity.rationale: Reservation, payments and table allocation software is standard engineering. Demand forecasting and integrations with restaurant operations add some difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Restaurants can switch booking tools, but guest data and prestige customer logos create some lock in. No network effect was shown in sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Global incumbents existed but no source shows them targeting Latin American fine dining. Meitre was still operating in listings and restaurant pages as of 2025.

market_need_then: YC's launch post says Meitre served half of the Latin America top 50 restaurants and cites tickets, deposits and card guarantees against no-shows, which points to a real pain around cancellations.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself. The name appears to echo the French maitre d' (an interpretation, not stated by a source) and is easy to misspell.

outcome_analysis: Meitre remains active and has not been acquired. It positioned itself as OpenTable for top restaurants, won marquee Latin American customers and raised a $1.6M seed from Andreessen Horowitz in May 2019. No later rounds are public, so growth beyond a niche is unproven.
notes: Meitre home page fetch returned only a title. Contxto says Meitre was in YC Winter 2019 while YC lists W18; the YC page is used. Aggregators show founding year 2016 or 2017 and total funding of $1.72M to $2.1M with investors such as Canary Ventures and 500 Startups; these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. Name origin and prior employers of the founders were not found. Press describes Meitre as Uruguayan, YC lists San Francisco.
